items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to compliance with the national driver register
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5842

TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to compliance
with the national driver register

PURPOSE:

This bill would require the department of motor vehicles to re-issue
drivers licenses, at no cost to licensees, which comply with the 2005
Federal Real ID Act, so that a New York drivers license will be an
acceptable form of identification for purpose of boarding an aircraft
or gaining admittance in to a federal facility. Without this
legislation, federal law will require New Yorkers to purchase a
passport or an enhanced ID if they wish to travel via aircraft or if
they wish to enter a federal facility.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1. Adds a new section to the Vehicle and Traffic Law requiring
DMV to issue drivers licenses which are compliant with the federal
Real ID Act. Further, this section requires the Commissioner of DMV to
file an annual report with the legislature regarding any and all other
federal laws or regulations, which the department has failed to comply
with.

Section 2 is the effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:

New York is one of the few states in our nation, along with New
Hampshire, Minnesota, Louisiana, Arizona and the American Samoa, that
has failed to comply with the provisions of the Federal Real ID Act.
The Federal Real ID Act was passed by Congress, and signed in to law
in 2005. The intent of the Act is to improve the reliability and
accuracy of state-issued identification documents, which serve to
inhibit terrorists' ability to evade detection by using fraudulent
identification. New York has failed to institute a system to verify
the authenticity of the documents that licensees provide them, and is
therefore non-compliant with this Act. New York has, however, The
unilateral decision by the New York State Department of Motor Vehicles
to fail to comply with this Act over the course of the last ten years
will have serious impacts on the citizens of our state in the coming
years, as the Act prohibits the federal government, or any entity
controlled by the federal government, from accepting drivers licenses
and ID cards unless they meet the minimum standards established by
this act.

Federal agencies will be prohibited from accepting for official uses
driver's licenses and identity cards issued by non-compliant states.
"Official Uses" is defined as accessing Federal facilities, entering
nuclear power plants, and boarding federally-regulated commercial
aircraft. The final phase of the enforcement schedule, the phase
involving the boarding of a federally regulated commercial aircraft,
is scheduled to take effect no sooner than 2016. Unless New York
complies prior to the enforcement of this last provision, New Yorkers


will need to show a second form of identification, either an enhanced
driver's license or a passport, in order to board an aircraft. This
additional requirement will certainly come as an additional cost to
all New Yorkers unless our State Department of Motor Vehicles takes
immediate action.

This bill directs New York State DMV to issue Real ID compliant
identification documentation to every entitled New Yorker, at no
additional cost to the licensee. Further, this bill requires DMV to
report annually to the Governor and the Legislature regarding any
federal laws or regulations which it has failed to comply with. In
addition to the inconvenience and financial costs that New Yorkers
will suffer as a result of DMV failing to take steps to comply with
this act, this is a serious homeland security concern. DMV should not
be making unilateral decisions regarding which federal laws it chooses
to follow, and which federal laws it chooses not to follow.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill

FISCAL IMPACT ON THE STATE:

None.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This act shall take immediately.

A.actClause: AN ACT to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to compliance with the federal Real ID Act
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S5842A

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to compliance
with the federal Real ID Act

 PURPOSE :

This bill would require the department of motor vehicles to re-issue
drivers licenses, at no cost to licensees, which comply with the 2005
Federal Real ID Act, so that a New York drivers license will be an
acceptable form of identification for purpose of boarding an aircraft
or gaining admittance in to a federal facility. Without this
legislation, federal law will require New Yorkers to purchase a
passport or an enhanced ID if they wish to travel via aircraft or if
they wish to enter a federal facility in the near future.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1. Provides that this Act shall be known as the "New York
Remembers Act".

Section 2. Legislative Intent

Section 3. Adds a new section to the Vehicle and Traffic Law requiring
DMV to issue drivers licenses which are compliant with the federal
Real ID Act. Any individual who wishes to have their current driver's
license upgraded to a Real ID compliant version, would be entitled to
do so at no additional cost. DMV would be required to submit fiscal
reports concerning any additional costs incurred as a result of this
measure, so that the state may explore reimbursement opportunities.

Section 4. This section requires the Commissioner of DMV to file an
annual report with the legislature regarding any and all other federal
laws or regulations, which the department has failed to comply with.

Section 5 is the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

The federal Real ID Act, which was passed by Congress and signed into
law in 2005, is a coordinated effort by the states and federal
government, intended to improve reliability and accuracy of
state-issued identification documents, which serve to inhibit a
terrorist's ability to evade detection by using fraudulent
identification. The standards established by the federal Real ID Act
resulted from a Congressional study investigating the various factors
which led to the horrific tragedy that occurred on September 11, 2001.
In addition to developing tamper proof technologies within the
identification card itself, states were directed to initiate a process
whereby the documentation submitted by an individual applying for a
state issued driver's license could be verified as authentic. The
purpose of the verification requirement is to ensure that terrorists
are not issued identification cards based on the proffering of forged
or otherwise fake documentation.

Until October 2015, New York State was one of only four states that
were deemed non-compliant with this federal homeland security law.
After ten years of non-compliance, and only after public outcry over
the impending enforcement deadlines, DMV finally submitted a
compliance waiver to the federal Department of Homeland Security.
While the waiver was approved, DMV was only given one year to bring
our state in to compliance. In addition to the security threat that
further delay in compliance presents, failure to take swift action by
the October 2016 deadline could again result in New Yorkers being
denied admittance to federal facilities and military bases, and could
even inhibit our ability to board an aircraft if Real ID becomes fully
enforced.

It is important to note that our DMV is, and has always been,
empowered via current statutory authority, to fully implement this
federal law. Unfortunately, until applying for the recent waiver, they
consciously chose not to comply, disregarding homeland security
concerns and leaving New Yorkers wondering if our IDs would be
accepted by the federal government.  DMV should not be making
unilateral decisions regarding which federal laws it chooses to
follow, and which federal laws it chooses not to follow. Especially
when their unilateral decision impacts our security as a state and the
ability of our citizens to travel or enter federally regulated
facilities.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New bill

 FISCAL IMPACT ON THE STATE :

None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the one hundred twentieth day after it
shall have become law. Effective immediately, the department of motor
vehicles shall begin promulgating rules and regulations to effectuate
the provisions of this act.
